{{Current events|year=2025|month=05|day=23|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
***After the [[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)#April / May: SAF final offensive|capture of Omdurman]] and the consequent end of the battle of [[Khartoum]], [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] find a [[mass grave]] with around 465 bodies located in Omdurman. [https://northafricapost.com/87267-sudans-army-claims-rsf-mass-graves-were-discovered-in-omdurman.html (The North Africa Post)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Prisoners of war in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Russia]] and [[Ukraine]] begin the largest [[prisoner exchange]] since the war began in February 2022, consisting of three days and 1,000 [[prisoners of war]] from each side. [https://www.npr.org/2025/05/23/nx-s1-5408714/ukraine-russia-prisoners-exchange (NPR)] [https://www.cnn.com/2025/05/23/europe/ukraine-and-russia-biggest-prisoner-exchange-war-intl (CNN)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[European Union–United States relations]], [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration]]
**[[U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] announces the implementation of 50% [[tariff]]s on all goods imported from [[European Union]] countries starting June 1. As a result, major [[Europe]]an [[stock exchange]]s like the [[Germany|German]] [[DAX]], the [[France|French]] [[CAC 40]], and the [[United Kingdom|British]] [[FTSE 100]] reported losses. [https://www.dw.com/en/trump-calls-for-50-tariffs-on-eu-imports-from-june-1/a-72648246 (DW)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 260 miners are trapped after a [[mining accident|collapse]] at the [[KDC mine|KDC]] [[gold mining|gold mine]] near [[Carletonville]], [[Gauteng]], [[South Africa]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/rescue-efforts-underway-260-workers-trapped-south-african-122105145 (ABC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[Minister of State for the Armed Forces]] of the [[United Kingdom]] says that the UK "does not recognize" the comments made by [[Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] yesterday, where he accused [[British prime minister]] [[Keir Starmer]], along with [[French president]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] and [[Canadian prime minister]] [[Mark Carney]] of "siding with [[Hamas]]" and being on "the wrong side of humanity". [https://news.sky.com/story/israel-gaza-latest-youre-on-wrong-side-of-humanity-netanyahu-launches-attack-on-starmer-after-killings-in-us-13362469 (Sky News)]
*[[Guyana–Venezuela territorial dispute]]
**[[Guyana|Guyanese]] Foreign Minister [[Hugh Todd]] says that [[Guyana]] will defend its sovereignty in face of [[Venezuela]]'s referendum next Sunday, passing a motion in parliament and reaffirming warnings by Guyana military chief [[Omar Khan (military)|Omar Khan]] that [[Venezuelans]] voting in the referendum in Guyana will be "immediately deported". [https://newsroom.gy/2025/05/23/guyana-will-not-be-bullied-threatened-or-intimidated-parliament-debates-motion-on-sovereignty/ (News Room Guyana)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024–2025 Georgian protests]]
**A court in [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] places opposition figure [[Zurab Japaridze]], leader of the country's largest opposition group [[Coalition for Change (Georgia)|Coalition for Change]], in [[pre-trial detention]] after the group led protests against the [[government of Georgia (country)|current government]] and the ruling party [[Georgian Dream]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/georgia-jails-opposition-leader-amid-crackdown-on-dissent/a-72639056 (DW)]
*[[2025 killing of Israeli Embassy in Washington, D.C. workers]]
**The suspect in the killing of two [[Embassy of Israel, Washington, D.C.|Israeli embassy]] workers in [[Washington, D.C.]] two days ago, is charged with two counts of [[Murder in the United States#degrees|first-degree]] [[murder]] along with other charges both federally and locally. [https://www.npr.org/2025/05/22/nx-s1-5407572/israeli-embassy-staffers-killed-washington-dc (NPR)]
*Authorities from [[Canada]], [[Denmark]], [[France]], [[Germany]], [[the Netherlands]], the United Kingdom, and the U.S. announce a joint operation to crack down on [[malware]] around the world, which took down over 300 [[server (computing)|servers]], neutralized 650 [[domain name|domains]], and seized over {{Euro}}3.5 million (US$3.9 million) of [[cryptocurrency]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/global-operation-takes-down-dangerous-malware-network/a-72643612 (DW)]
*[[2025 Hamburg stabbing attack]]
**A [[mass stabbing]] takes place at the [[Hamburg Hauptbahnhof|main train station]] in [[Hamburg]], Germany, injuring eightteen people, including four critically. A woman was arrested at the scene. [https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/regional/hamburg/hamburg-hauptbahnhof-messerangriff-100.html (Tagesschau)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[United States district judge]] [[Allison D. Burroughs]] from the [[United States District Court for the District of Massachusetts|District of Massachussetts]] blocks [[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|homeland security secretary]] [[Kristi Noem]]'s order to disallow [[Harvard University]] from enrolling [[international students]]. [https://apnews.com/article/harvard-foreign-students-enrollment-trump-lawsuit-94b65866c563e67a7a7a3c79e90144d6 (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2024–25 Serie A]]
**In [[association football]], [[SSC Napoli]] wins their fourth [[Lega Serie A|Serie A]] title and the second title in three seasons after defeating [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] 2–0 in the final matchday. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c1derv64npqt (BBC)]
